title: review: E3 fix round 1: rebase the committed gate hook onto goal/T-0201 with the test fix, re-gate (T-0229 held gate_red)
spec: T-0229 (E3 v2 Jev tool-call gate) is committed as f1e17e2 on task/T-0229 (the Planner committed the executor's uncommitted worktree) and is held gate_red only because tests/test_jev.py depended on the committed pool.toml (fixed by P10 T-0236 on goal/T-0201). STEP 0: your worktree was cut from goal/T-0201; run `git reset --hard task/T-0229` and confirm `git log --oneline -1` shows f1e17e2. STEP 1: `git rebase goal/T-0201` (pool.toml may conflict on the [jev] table: keep both gate_mode from f1e17e2 and enabled = true from goal). STEP 2: run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh on the worktree; fix only what the gate reports inside the E3 scope (.claude/hooks/jev-gate.sh, orchestrator/jev_gate.py, tests/test_jev_gate.py, .claude/settings.json, .orchestrator/pool.toml). STEP 3: run one real hook invocation as a smoke test: pipe a PreToolUse JSON {tool_name: "Read", tool_input: {file_path: "README.md"}, session_id: "smoke", transcript_path: "/nonexistent"} with ORCH_TASK_ID set to this task's id into .claude/hooks/jev-gate.sh and confirm exit 0 and one appended line in .orchestrator/runs/jev/gate.jsonl with scored true (the key is in the Keychain; jev enabled). Report the p_needed value in the summary. Commit when green.
acceptance: git log on the task branch contains f1e17e2 (or its rebased equivalent with the same title) on top of goal/T-0201 head
The smoke invocation appended one scored line to .orchestrator/runs/jev/gate.jsonl and the summary states p_needed

comments.issue: Registering this hook on Bash|Read|Grep|Glob|Edit|Write|WebFetch|WebSearch makes every one of those calls in every executor session (jev.enabled is already true in pool.toml) do a synchronous uv-run round trip plus a network call to Jev, twice per call (one for --enabled, one for the real ask). In gate_mode=log this buys no blocking benefit yet, only latency and daily_budget_tokens burn. Not a correctness bug against the stated acceptance criteria, but worth flagging as a cost/latency risk before this rides to main.

_PROTECTED_BASH_RES only exempts git commit/add/status/diff/log and tests-green.sh from scoring; other frequently-repeated read-only git commands (e.g. git show, git branch, git log --oneline variants already covered) aren't in scope here so no action needed, just noting the allowlist is narrow by design.
